channel.title: On the Pulse — Debbie Tan
channel.description: A monthly read on AI, data, measurement and privacy.

item.title: October 2026: AI labs kept shipping. Google quietly took control.
item.description: Here's the one-line version: OpenAI and Anthropic both released new things this month, nothing in our stack broke, but Google quietly moved who controls your measurement data from Analytics into Ads. That's the one to actually act on. Everything else below is useful context.

item.title: August 2026: Google quietly made AI Max mandatory for most Search campaigns
item.description: Google quietly made its AI system the default for how most Search campaigns run, effective this week — with no public announcement, no rollback, and notification by email alone. Nielsen closed on absorbing one of only two independent ad-verification vendors with real scale. Peer-reviewed research shows platform-reported lift can overstate true impact by a factor of 13. And new WARC data puts hard numbers on why social-first budget strategies are hitting a ceiling. Every item below earned its place on merit, not just because it happened in the window.
